details.label: Summary
details.text: Developing thunderstorms may continue to evolve into a better organized cluster through 6-8 AM CDT. Eventually, this probably will become accompanied by increasing potential for strong to severe surface gusts, though how soon remains uncertain

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection continues to increase and intensify within a zone of stronger warm advection, along a tightening lower/mid-tropospheric baroclinic zone where seasonably high moisture content is supporting large CAPE, beneath the northern periphery of a plume of elevated mixed-layer air. Strongest storms, now focused south of Sioux Falls SD into the Storm Lake IA vicinity, have yet to organize or generate a notable surface pressure perturbation. However, this may begin to change over the next few hours. While there is considerable spread within convection-allowing guidance, of perhaps particular note, the latest Rapid Refresh output suggests that continuing intensifying thunderstorm development may become accompanied by the evolution of a strengthening lower/mid-tropospheric cyclonic circulation, based on its depiction of strengthening rear inflow to 50-60+ kt in the 700-500 mb layer through 11-13Z. This would probably be accompanied by increasing potential for strong to severe surface gusts at some point, though how soon remains unclear given the initially stable near-surface lapse rates
